resolved_by: U.S.S.G. supp. to app. C, amend. 693 (2006), which amended Note 1 to § 3C1.1 to adopt the majority view that pre-investigative obstructive conduct may be covered if purposefully calculated, and likely, to thwart the investigation or prosecution of the offense of conviction
issue: Can obstructive conduct that occurred before the investigation of the offense of conviction began support a U.S.S.G. § 3C1.1 obstruction-of-justice enhancement?
quote: The Sentencing Commission added this language to Note 1 in 2006 to “address[] a circuit conflict regarding the issue of whether pre-investigative conduct can form the basis of an adjustment under §3C1.1.”
cite: United States v. Kay, No. 24-4018 (10th Cir. 2025)
